stories.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, the inference stack behind its production service

key_facts.fact: On Oct 20, 2026, DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, its in-house inference framework that powers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at scale, saying it wants to help the community lower compute costs and energy use.
key_facts.excerpt: Introducing DeepInfer, our in-house inference framework, now fully open source! Powering DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at scale with high throughput and low latency. We're sharing our production stack to help the community lower compute costs, reduce energy use, and make AI more affordable.

key_facts.fact: DeepInfer is released under the Apache 2.0 license and supports NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: License: Apache License 2.0 ... Supported hardware: NVIDIA SM100 GPUs; Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

key_facts.fact: Features include optimized kernels (FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP), MoE expert parallelism, speculative decoding with draft tokens, SWA bounded replay, batch-invariant inference, deterministic sampling and structured outputs.
key_facts.excerpt: Optimized kernels: FlashMLA, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, DeepSelect ... DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification ... SWA bounded replay ... Batch-invariant inference ... Deterministic sampling ... Structured outputs

key_facts.fact: The release omits a KV cache system, prefill/decode disaggregation and load balancing across replicas, so it is not a complete serving stack.
key_facts.excerpt: Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release): A KV cache system; VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation ...; Load balancing across data-parallel replicas

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek said inference code for its future models will also be published in DeepInfer, and it separately open-sourced deepseek-recipe, its production token encoding/decoding component aligned with the official API.
key_facts.excerpt: Inference code for future DeepSeek models and ongoing optimizations will land here too.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg framed the release as potentially making DeepSeek's technology cheaper and easier for businesses to run.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek is opening up the software it uses to run its artificial intelligence models at scale, potentially making its technology cheaper and easier for businesses to run.

stories.headline: Inception releases Mercury 3, a diffusion LLM running at 1,000+ tokens per second

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, 2026, Inception released Mercury 3, which CEO Stefano Ermon called the most intelligent diffusion LLM ever released, claiming it outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on quality while running at over 1,000 tokens per second.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're releasing Mercury 3. Mercury 3 is by far our most powerful model and the most intelligent diffusion LLM ever released. It outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on quality while running at 1000+ tok/sec. — Stefano Ermon, October 19, 2026

key_facts.fact: Unlike autoregressive models that generate one token at a time, Mercury 3 generates and refines multiple tokens in parallel; Inception claims it is 4x to 8x faster than Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and GLM-5.3 Flash while beating them on agentic benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Inception claims that Mercury 3 performs 4x to 8x faster than Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, and GLM-5.3 Flash while performing better than all of them on agentic benchmarks.

key_facts.fact: On Inception's own benchmark table, Mercury 3 leads GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 on 8 of 12 tests, including SWE-Bench Atlas (51.08 vs 33.33 and 32.26), but trails Haiku 5.5 on DeepSWE v1 (46.31 vs 51.62).
key_facts.excerpt: Leads 8 of 12 benchmarks vs GPT-6 Luna and Haiku 5.5 (self-reported, medium settings). Best: SWE-Bench Atlas 51.08, about 18 points ahead of both rivals. Worst: DeepSWE v1 46.31, 5.31 points behind Haiku 5.5 (51.62).

key_facts.fact: Mercury 3 has a 1M-token context window and more than 40 times the parameters of Mercury 1; Inception did not disclose the parameter count.
key_facts.excerpt: Size: Parameters not disclosed. Inception says it is more than 40x larger than Mercury 1. Context is 1M tokens.

key_facts.fact: Launch pricing is $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens, 50% off the list price of $0.20/$0.70.
key_facts.excerpt: List pricing is $0.20 per 1M input and $0.70 per 1M output tokens. At launch it is 50% off: $0.10 and $0.35.

key_facts.fact: Inception said it used swarms of Mercury 3 agents for recursive self-improvement, which increased the model's overall speed by 16% beyond the upgrades made by its team.
key_facts.excerpt: Inception also reported that it implemented swarms of Mercury 3 agents for recursive self improvement where they increased the overall speed of the model by 16% on top of the upgrades made by the Inception team itself.

key_facts.fact: Mercury 3 is available via the Inception API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel; it is API-only with no open weights.
key_facts.excerpt: Mercury 3 is live on the Inception API Platform, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel.

stories.headline: OpenAI says its new models jump in COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic coding and migration

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, 2026, OpenAI said its latest models bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic, which power software that banks, governments and businesses depend on.
key_facts.excerpt: Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. These languages power software that banks, governments, and businesses depend on.

key_facts.fact: On OpenAI's new MultiLangBench, which asks a model to build a SQLite-compatible database engine in 20 languages, GPT-6 Astra averaged an 87.4% test pass rate, up from 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol; COBOL rose from 10.9% to 72.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: It said GPT-6 Astra had an average test pass rate of 87.4 percent across 20 languages, making it a lot of effective than GPT-5.6 Sol that had a 26.8 percent pass rate. COBOL remains the hardest language to crack, with Astra's pass rate being 72 percent.

key_facts.fact: On a COBOL migration test to C++, Java, Kotlin, Python or Rust requiring byte-for-byte output parity, GPT-6.1 Sol scored 86.6% at low reasoning effort versus 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 97.9% at higher effort.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Sol scored 86.6% on COBOL migration at low effort. GPT-5.6 Sol scored 5.4% at the same setting, and GPT-6.1 Sol did it at 61% of the API cost. At higher reasoning effort, accuracy reached 97.9%

key_facts.fact: GPT-6 Luna reached 40.3% on MultiLangBench at an estimated $0.77 per sample, about 78% cheaper than GPT-5.6 Sol's $3.48.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 Luna reached 40.3% at an estimated average API cost of $0.77 per sample, compared with $3.48 for GPT-5.6 Sol, about 78% lower.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI cites COBOL as supporting more than 40% of online banking systems and 95% of ATM transactions, and is releasing MultiLangBench on GitHub; it says production migrations still require expert review.
key_facts.excerpt: COBOL supports more than 40% of online banking systems, 80% of in-person credit card transactions and 95% of ATM transactions ... On its new MultiLangBench evaluation, which OpenAI is releasing on GitHub

stories.headline: US DHS orders DeepSeek technology removed from federal civilian IT systems

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, 2026, DHS made public an order requiring federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek technology from their IT systems and barring future purchases of its products and services.
key_facts.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security has ordered federal civilian agencies to remove artificial-intelligence technology developed by China's DeepSeek from their information technology systems. The order also bars future purchases of DeepSeek's products and services

key_facts.fact: The order, issued under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018, also covers DeepSeek affiliates and third-party products and services built using DeepSeek implementations.
key_facts.excerpt: Pursuant to the authority granted by the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018 ... removal of all DeepSeek and DeepSeek affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.

key_facts.fact: The order was originally issued on July 24 and applies to civilian agencies including Treasury, State and Justice, but excludes the Department of Defense; agencies can request exceptions within 60 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The order, originally issued on July 24, applies to federal civilian agencies, including the Treasury, State and Justice departments, but it excludes the Department of Defense.

key_facts.fact: DHS said DeepSeek models present 'multiple threat vectors' and that use 'may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC', and that the models may contain malware or security vulnerabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees or vendors."

key_facts.fact: Several US agencies, including Commerce and the Navy, and states such as New York, Tennessee and Virginia had previously restricted DeepSeek on government devices.
key_facts.excerpt: Previously, several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned the use of DeepSeek on government devices. Multiple states, including New York, Tennessee and Virginia, have taken similar steps.

stories.headline: Safety advocates slam Anthropic's leaked federal AI bill; company says it will revise it

key_facts.fact: A discussion draft of a federal AI bill Anthropic had circulated to lawmakers, published by Politico on Friday Oct 16, drew broad criticism from AI safety advocates as weaker than the bipartisan FRONTIER Act; Transformer published an analysis on Oct 19.
key_facts.excerpt: A leaked discussion draft of a federal AI bill which Anthropic has been circulating to lawmakers, published by Politico on Friday ... has been widely criticized by AI safety advocates, is much weaker than the Obernolte/Trahan FRONTIER Act

key_facts.fact: The draft requires third-party evaluators to assess catastrophic risk but sets no standards or licensing for them, allowing self-certification.
key_facts.excerpt: Like the FRONTIER Act, it requires third-party evaluators to assess AI companies' models and practices for catastrophic risk. Unlike FRONTIER, however, there are no standards or licensing requirements for evaluators, which can self-certify.

key_facts.fact: To block a dangerous model, the Commerce Department would have to petition a federal court, which decides 'without deference' and must weigh the harm a blocking order would cause to the developer.
key_facts.excerpt: If the Commerce Department ... wants to stop one, it must petition a federal court ... The court decides every question "without deference" ... It must also "consider the harm the [blocking] order would cause to the frontier developer, to users, and to the public."

key_facts.fact: The bill would preempt state frontier-AI laws such as California's SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act while carving out child safety laws.
key_facts.excerpt: laws like California's SB 53, New York's RAISE and Illinois' SB 315 that seek to govern "frontier AI" would be preempted, while child safety and other laws are explicitly carved out.

key_facts.fact: On Oct 19, Anthropic's head of federal affairs Anthony Cimino said the text was an early draft, that it does not absolve companies of liability, and that Anthropic wants to work with policymakers to make it 'as strong as it can be'; he had earlier said the preemption language would be adjusted.
key_facts.excerpt: This was our early draft proposal for addressing specific types of catastrophic harm from AI at the federal level. We are not proposing it should be the sole accountability mechanism the government can use. Nor does the bill absolve companies of liability when they inflict harm. We are also interested in working with policymakers to revisit this to ensure it is as strong as it can be.

sources.title: Anthropic's weak AI bill undermines its 'safety first' approach
Tweet by @ajcimino: This was our early draft proposal for addressing specific types of catastrophic harm

stories.headline: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent order $35B+ of export-compliant Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 cards

key_facts.fact: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million of Nvidia's new RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards with a collective sticker price of over $35 billion, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters on Oct 20.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million of Nvidia's new RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards with a collective sticker price of over $35 billion, two people familiar with the matter said, in a rush for a less powerful but export-compliant chip amid US restrictions on trade with China.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia told customers and partners it cannot guarantee it can fill the orders; one source said partners might receive only 5% to 10% of quantities requested, and another said Nvidia could produce no more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards globally in 2027. Total orders from China exceeded 6 million.
key_facts.excerpt: One source said Nvidia told partners they might receive only 5% to 10% of the quantities requested. Another said the company had indicated it could produce no more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards globally in 2027. Total orders from customers in China have exceeded 6 million, two of the sources said.

key_facts.fact: The cards are priced at about $11,400 each; the RTX PRO 5500 is a workstation chip, less powerful than the H200 and B300, and Chinese buyers want it mainly for AI inference.
key_facts.excerpt: The three Chinese tech giants' orders are for cards priced at about $11,400 each... Chinese companies are seeking to use the cards primarily for AI inference

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's Blackwell-based B300 cannot be sold to Chinese buyers under US export controls, while H200 exports are reviewed case by case and subject to licensing conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's Blackwell-based B300 data-centre chip is not allowed to be sold to Chinese buyers under US export controls, while exports of its Hopper-based H200 are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to licensing conditions.

key_facts.fact: Starting in 2027 Nvidia is expected to devote much of its TSMC capacity to its Rubin data-center platform; customers were told to expect early RTX PRO 5500 samples in December and commercial deliveries from Q1 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting in 2027, Nvidia is expected to devote much of its capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co to Rubin... Nvidia has told customers to expect early samples in December, with commercial deliveries beginning in the first quarter of 2027

key_facts.fact: An Nvidia spokesperson blamed 'outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China's own limit on US imports' for restricting US firms.
key_facts.excerpt: "US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China's own limit on US imports," the spokesperson said.

stories.headline: Meta details Prometheus, its Ohio supercluster headed to ~1M GPUs, with reliability data

key_facts.fact: In an engineering post on Oct 19, Meta said the first phase of Prometheus, its gigawatt-scale supercluster in New Albany, Ohio, is complete and trained the Muse family of models, including Muse Wonder.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has published a detailed look at Prometheus, its gigawatt-scale AI supercluster in New Albany, Ohio. The first phase is complete and was used to train the Muse family of foundation models, including the Muse Wonder frontier models.

key_facts.fact: Prometheus today spans hundreds of thousands of GPUs across multiple buildings, including rapid-deployment structures and leased capacity, and will reach roughly 1 million GPUs at full scale.
key_facts.excerpt: Prometheus spans "hundreds of thousands of GPUs" across several buildings... At full scale it will hold "roughly 1 million distributed GPUs, all functioning in lockstep".

key_facts.fact: The cluster runs Nvidia GB200 NVL72 (Catalina) and GB300 NVL72 (Clemente) racks, with Vera Rubin NVL72 (San Miguel) racks of over 170 kW, fully liquid-cooled, arriving next; each 72-GPU rack trains on 64 GPUs and keeps 8 as spares.
key_facts.excerpt: Prometheus runs two NVIDIA platforms: Catalina, built on GB200 NVL72... and Clemente, built on GB300 NVL72... A third, San Miguel, based on NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 with fully liquid-cooled racks of over 170 kW, is arriving next. Each 72-GPU domain trains on a 64-GPU slice and keeps eight GPUs as in-rack spares

key_facts.fact: Interruptions peaked at nearly 1,000 a day per 8,000 GPUs when the cluster came online in mid-2025; a year of work cut that by 99%, and Muse Wonder pre-training ran above 85% goodput with ~47,000 GPU hours between interruptions, since raised above 54,000.
key_facts.excerpt: When Prometheus first came online in mid-2025, Meta says interruptions peaked at nearly 1,000 a day for every 8,000 GPUs. A year of work... cut that by 99%... more than 85% "goodput" for pre-training... about 47,000 GPU hours between interruptions, since raised to over 54,000.

key_facts.fact: Synchronized GPU workloads cause 30-40% power swings; Meta manages them with software called Dynamo Dimmer plus rack batteries and site-level storage.
key_facts.excerpt: Prometheus produces power swings of 30% to 40%... Meta handles this with software called Dynamo Dimmer, which gradually lowers GPU power limits as the cluster nears its electrical ceiling... backed by rack batteries, capacitor trays and site-level battery storage.

key_facts.fact: Prometheus is the blueprint for Hyperion, Meta's next supercluster in Richland Parish, Louisiana, designed with closed-loop liquid cooling and a full grid connection through Entergy paid for by Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: Prometheus is the blueprint for Hyperion, Meta's next supercluster in Richland Parish, Louisiana, which is being designed with closed-loop liquid cooling and a full grid connection through utility Entergy, paid for by Meta.

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday, October 20, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers were set ablaze and halted after hitting IRGC naval mines at what Tehran calls an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: "Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the Guards said in a statement published on their official Sepah News website.

key_facts.fact: Iran International reported the IRGC Navy said the two tankers hit mines on Monday night (October 19), did not identify the vessels or report casualties, and warned that ships crossing the mined passage could be set ablaze.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's IRGC Navy said on Tuesday that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in a passage south of the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, and were stopped... It warned that ships crossing the mined passage could be set ablaze, but did not identify the tankers or report any casualties.

key_facts.fact: The Guards also said they shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone; this came a day after the IRGC said another tanker caught fire after hitting a mine, and two days after it said two other tankers had hit mines.
key_facts.excerpt: The Revolutionary Guards also said they had shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone. On Monday, the Guards said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine, while the day before it said two other tankers had hit mines.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper said the strait is controlled by the US and regional partners and 'remains open for business,' citing about 400 merchant ship transits in the previous week.

key_facts.fact: The UK will also provide an RAF A400M transport aircraft, military advisers to Saudi staff officers, and an extension of air-to-air refuelling support for Saudi air operations, including those to degrade Houthi targets in Yemen.

stories.headline: Japan launches MMX, first mission aiming to bring back samples from Mars' moon Phobos

key_facts.fact: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft launched on October 19 at 3:41 p.m. EDT (19:41 GMT) on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center, the 10th H3 flight.
key_facts.excerpt: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off ... at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket

key_facts.fact: JAXA confirmed the probe separated from the rocket over an hour after liftoff and was 'beginning its journey towards the Martian system'; arrival near Mars is expected around August 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Over an hour later, JAXA announced during the livestream that the probe had successfully separated from the H3 and was "beginning its journey towards the Martian system". The spacecraft is due to arrive near Mars around August next year

key_facts.fact: MMX plans two touchdowns on Phobos to collect at least 10 grams of soil, with the sample capsule due to land in Australia in 2031; it would be the first sample return from a Martian moon.
key_facts.excerpt: MMX will perform two separate touchdowns on Phobos to collect and stow samples in the spacecraft's return capsule... If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule will land in Australia in 2031.

key_facts.fact: The spacecraft carries the German-French Idefix rover (DLR and CNES), set to land on Phobos around the turn of 2028/2029 and become the first rover to drive on a Martian moon, exploring for about 100 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The Idefix rover, developed jointly by DLR and CNES, is scheduled to land on Mars' moon Phobos around the turn of the year 2028/2029 and explore it for approximately 100 days.

key_facts.fact: NASA has invested about $87 million through the end of the mission and will receive at least 15% of the planned 10-gram Phobos sample; it contributed the MEGANE spectrometer and a Honeybee Robotics pneumatic sampler.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA has also invested approximately $87 million through the end of the mission... At least 15% of the planned 10-gram (0.35 ounces) returned Phobos sample will be reserved for NASA's study.

key_facts.fact: China's Tianwen-3 is scheduled to launch around 2028 and aims to return Mars samples as early as 2031, potentially before the Japanese mission.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and aims to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 — potentially before the Japanese mission's return.

stories.headline: FDA approves GSK's Jemperli as first immunotherapy for some locally advanced rectal cancers

key_facts.fact: On October 19, the FDA granted accelerated approval to GSK's Jemperli (dostarlimab) alone for adults with previously untreated stage II or III locally advanced rectal cancer whose tumors are mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H).
key_facts.excerpt: Today's approval is for Jemperli used alone in adults with previously untreated stage II or stage III locally advanced rectal cancer... patients' tumors must be mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H), as determined by an FDA-authorized test.

key_facts.fact: In the 154-patient phase 2 AZUR-1 trial, after median follow-up of more than two years almost three-fourths of patients had not needed surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA based its decision on interim results from AZUR-1... in 154 patients... After a median follow-up of more than 2 years... almost three-fourths of patients had not needed surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: GSK said 68% of evaluable patients achieved a sustained clinical complete response at 12 months by investigator assessment (47% by independent central review, data still maturing), with no recurrences among responders to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Investigator-assessed data... showed 68% of evaluable patients (98/144...) achieved cCR12... 47% (54/116)... of evaluable patients have achieved cCR12... No disease recurrences have been reported among responders to date, after a median follow up of more than two years.

key_facts.fact: The MSI-H/dMMR biomarker is found in around 5-10% of rectal cancers; standard treatment of chemotherapy, radiation and surgery can cause lasting bowel, urinary and sexual dysfunction and infertility.
key_facts.excerpt: Current standard of treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer includes chemotherapy, radiation and surgery, but these can have lasting consequences, including bowel, urinary and sexual dysfunction, secondary cancers and infertility. For patients with MSI-H/dMMR tumors, a biomarker found in around 5-10% of rectal cancers

key_facts.fact: The review ran under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program and the approval came 4 months ahead of the FDA goal date.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved this application 4 months ahead of the FDA goal date. This application is part of the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher (CNPV) pilot program

key_facts.fact: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 20% of patients and 3% discontinued treatment; GSK will present full AZUR-1 interim data at the ESMO Congress in October 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 20% of patients receiving Jemperli... Jemperli was permanently discontinued due to adverse reactions in 3% of patients. Full data from the AZUR-1 interim analysis will be presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in October 2026.

stories.headline: US sanctions China's MiraclePlus VC firm over ex-Google engineer's AI trade-secret theft

key_facts.fact: On October 19, the US State Department designated five China-based entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act (PAIPA): Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, venture firm MiraclePlus, and three MiraclePlus-linked funds and entities.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the Department of State announced the designations of five entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act (PAIPA) in connection with theft of trade secrets from U.S. persons.

key_facts.fact: Zhisuan was founded in 2023 by former Google engineer Linwei Ding, who pitched MiraclePlus's incubator by claiming Zhisuan could replicate Google's AI infrastructure; MiraclePlus gave seed capital in exchange for a stake.
key_facts.excerpt: Ding applied on behalf of Zhisuan to a China-based startup incubation program known as MiraclePlus, touting his experience with and knowledge of Google's technology and internal systems and claiming that Zhisuan could replicate Google's SI infrastructure technology... MiraclePlus gave seed capital in exchange for an ownership stake in Zhisuan.

key_facts.fact: Ding was convicted on January 29 of seven counts of economic espionage and seven counts of theft of trade secrets; he was sentenced to a year in jail in September.
key_facts.excerpt: Ding, also known as Leon Ding, was convicted on Jan. 29 of seven counts of economic espionage and seven counts of theft of trade secrets, according to a DOJ press release.

key_facts.fact: Sanctions include property blocking, banking and foreign-exchange restrictions, a cap on US loans above $10 million in 12 months, and a ban on US persons buying significant equity or debt; OFAC allowed wind-down of MiraclePlus dealings until January 19, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: the PAIPA sanctions apply to all five entities include property blocking and transaction prohibitions... restrictions on foreign-exchange and banking transactions... a prohibition on U.S. financial institutions providing loans or credit totaling more than $10 million in any 12-month period... General License 2 authorizes transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to wind down dealings involving MiraclePlus... through 12:01 a.m. ET on Jan. 19.

key_facts.fact: MiraclePlus was founded by former Microsoft and Baidu AI executive Lu Qi as the successor to Y Combinator's abandoned China program, and has backed SiliconFlow and robotics maker AgiBot, both considering Hong Kong listings.
key_facts.excerpt: Lu's MiraclePlus, the successor to a Chinese program run by Silicon Valley's Y Combinator, and three affiliates drew sanctions for providing seed financing to Zhisuan... It's since backed some of China's most promising startups, including AI inference platform SiliconFlow and robotics maker AgiBot, both of which are considering Hong Kong listings.
